He signed with Philadelphia as an undrafted free agent, fought his way into a starting job, helped the Eagles win Super Bowl LIX, and was later named a team captain.

Four years later, he signed a three-year, $24.75 million contract with the Houston Texans.

AJ Green went undrafted in 2022. Three years later, he signed a four-year, $45 million extension with the Milwaukee Bucks.

Green was a four-star recruit out of high school, choosing Northern Iowa, where his dad was an assistant coach, over several Power 5 programs. He won Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year as a sophomore, then a hip injury ended his 2020–21 season after just three games.

He came back the next year and won the award again. Still, no team picked him in the 2022 NBA Draft.

The Bucks gave him a two-way contract. He turned it into a full-time roster spot in 2023, then signed the extension in 2025. That season, he broke Ray Allen’s franchise record for three-pointers in a season.

- Gold medal with Team USA

No one in NCAA softball history has ever thrown a pitch as fast as Karlyn Pickens.

She set the record at 78.2 mph in March 2025, then broke her own mark two months later at 79.4 mph. By the time she left Tennessee, she was one of the most dominant pitchers in college softball.

Before she'd even finished her senior season, the Carolina Blaze made her the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 AUSL College Draft. A few months into her pro career, she added another milestone—a gold medal with Team USA at the 2026 USA Softball International Cup.

In September, she helped Team USA punch its ticket to the 2027 World Cup Finals. None of it happens without years of training, recovery, and disciplined fueling behind the scenes. #BreakingBarriers
